customize.text: Character Story

<color=#ffd680>Character Story 3</color>
Around 2,600 years ago, the Archon War had yet to end, and the world had yet to fall under the dominion of The Seven.
In those days, the city called "Mondstadt" was surrounded on all sides by gales impenetrable even to the birds of the air. The wind's ceaseless howling ground the soil and the rock of that city into smooth, flowing dust.
The Lord of Wind who lived in his high tower was Decarabian, God of Storms. He squinted from on high at his subjects, who bowed before him in the unceasing wind, and, believing them submissive, thought this good.
In those days, Venti was but a single thread of the thousand winds that roared through the northern lands.
He who would in latter days be known as "Barbatos" was but a tiny elemental spirit, without a shred of divine dignity, a breeze that brought subtle changes for the better, or tiny seeds of hope.
In Mondstadt of old, Venti met a young boy. This lad knew how to play the lyre, and longed to write the greatest poem of all.
"I do so wish to see the birds in flight."
So said the boy who had never seen the blue sky, eagles, or the green grass, his voice almost utterly drowned by the wind.
"Friend, will you not come along?"

customize.text: Season Fortune Slip

"The walls circling the tower were too grand, too majestic, and so the bricks and tiles needed were as numerous as grains of sand upon a beach.
Surely, who would notice if a few sand grains were missing? So thinking, the artisan tarried.
He would do a little every day, note the work he had done, and leave the rest for tomorrow.
Yet, the 'tomorrows' left to him were numbered.
The warriors who lifted high rebellion's song would enter through those gaps, saving them seven-tenths of the losses they might have otherwise suffered storming the walls...
The artisan watched this from afar, the secret delight in his heart mixed with fear and apprehension.
Fortune had smiled upon him this time, for his laxity had inadvertently birthed great beneficence.
But what about next time?"
— The Ones the Wind Forgot: Decarabian's People
To cast one's hopes upon tomorrow in exchange for a brief moment of peace...
That something is tried and true is an intoxicating thought.
But what if the "you" of tomorrow is also waiting on opportunities created in the past?
Waiting for all the previously invested effort that has been built up for this moment to bring about some transformation?
This test of promise-keeping could only ever be approached one way.
Know that delay and regret are inseparable twins.
Perhaps it is best to take action immediately, both today and tomorrow.
Decarabian

More than three thousand years ago, the future Mondstadt, built on the ruins of Great Arcadia, was ruled by the God of Storms, Decarabian. When King of the North Winds, Andrius, who had come from the north to protect the oppressed people, waged war against King of the Tower, and Mondstadt was transformed into a vast icy wasteland, Decarabian was forced to retreat north to what is now known as Stormterror's Lair. He built a city in a ring shape, where every resident of the city had been arranged their own spot between the inner and outer rings. Right in the center of the city was the tall tower where the King of Gales resided. Decarabian erected a wall of storms around his capital, impenetrable to the King of the North Winds. The Lord of Wind was content with his capital and accepted the worship of the people from atop his tower. He believed he had protected his people, unaware that they did not bow to him out of respect or adoration, but because the harsh winds had laid them low. Such were the dreams and aspirations of the Lord of Wind, which might have lasted forever if not for the song of freedom that instantly destroyed the walls of his capital.
One day, the silent huntress, Amos, who once roosted with owls on withered boughs and danced with hawks across the plains, was sacrificed to the King of the Tower. The Lord of Wind, feared by all peoples, elevated her to the place of favored counsel, impressed by her mastery of archery. Amos believed that Decarabian was the first to show her tender words and teach her to understand love. Beneath the shadow of the towering spire, amidst a prison of delusive enchantment, the huntress believed herself cherished by a tyrant. And even when the God of Storms shorn the hands of a poor craftsman who had offered Amos a mechanical singing bird of pure gold with his sharp wind, the huntress remained faithful to her master. For her master and savior, she was ready to quench those fearful, loathing eyes and stain her fair hands with the blood of innocents.

<color=#ffffffd9>"My beloved master... Save you, none have shown me gentle dreams."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Neither the kiss of waves upon sand, nor greenwood's embrace of verdant earth."</color>

But no matter what victories she offered to her king, no matter how many rebel villages lay in ruins, no matter how many people she slaughtered in the dungeon, the King of the Tower never poured upon her the love he spoke of. Awoken from blind devotion, Amos suddenly realized that from the very first day they met until the end, her likeness was never mirrored in the depths of his eyes. And if neither dances offered beneath the veil of wind and gentle whispers could not earn her a moment of his gaze, if all bloodied glory and the delight of slaughter could not make him look only upon her, then let his gaze linger forever upon the moment her image was seared into it. It was the only love the Lord of Wind ever showed, for he spoke of love, but his words were accompanied only by razor winds. And until the moment when a mortal, who knew no love, and a god, who could not know it, tore each other apart, they never knew each other's hearts.

<color=#ffffffd9>"My beloved master... Save you, my heart shall love no other."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"So I beg you — look only upon me, none but me."</color>

In the early days, the people of Mondstadt had a tradition of building theaters on top of windy cliffs to please the gods, and they staged performances for them, for they believed the gods enjoyed stories and ballads. During Decarabian's reign, certain poems and melodies were banned, as discerning people could sense the spirit of resistance that lay behind the music of the bards and singers. Back then, everyone knew this song, and it was used to raise glasses and give farewells:

<color=#ffffffd9>"If someone plucks out your tongue, you can still sing with your eyes."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"If someone blinds you in both eyes, you can still see with your ears."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"If someone conspires to destroy tomorrow, then raise them a glass,"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"For even if tomorrow dies, this song shall live on."</color>

customize.text: Rebellion

When Decarabian ordered warriors who had never seen the sky to destroy the rebels in the cradle who were attempting to shake the tower, one of the warriors lowered his blade, hearing the songs flowing from the strings of a young bard. He was not deceived by the tongues of treachery or swayed by the promises of illusions. He yielded only to the caged bird's yearning for the sky, a hunger writ in the blood of every living creature. Thus, the silent, red-haired warrior cast aside both duty and name to gather the winds scattered across the long night for the boy singing to the dawn.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Let the nameless flowers kiss away your tears, and grieve not for the parting that tomorrow brings."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Until the breath of dawn erases my name, and reveals for you the light that is true."</color>

The father of the future head of Gunnhildr's Clan once served the King of the Tower, but when they could bear Decarabian's tyranny, he led his clan out of the city, to where ferocious winds howled without mercy. Life in the wasteland beyond the city gates was harsh and unforgiving, and those who escaped the wrath of a tyrant found themselves trapped amidst relentless and all-engulfing blizzards. Just when the people lost all hope, the spirit of a thousand winds heard Gunnhildr's prayers, and the sincere plea of the chief's young daughter and the cry for protection from the snow and winds became a faith. The faith gathered in front of the wind spirit like water flowing into a spring and became the source from which the wind spirit drew its power. The wind spirit used this power to make a small shelter for the clan, and bestowed upon the clan chief's daughter the power to protect. After her father's death, Gunnhildr took his place as the clan's leader, and from that day forth, she protected her clan faithfully. And when, two thousand six hundred years ago, people couldn't bear the tyranny, and a huntress, a warrior, a wind spirit, and a young bard challenged the merciless Decarabian, Gunnhildr led her people to make a stand against the God of Storms' fury. The weak and infirm who could not scale the tower instead sang the song that, till now, had only ever been whispered in corners where the wind did not reach, and that drinking song rose up with force enough to shake the city walls, spurring the heroes on as they climbed.

<color=#ffffffd9>"If someone plucks out your tongue, you can still sing with your eyes."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"If someone blinds you in both eyes, you can still see with your ears."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"But if anyone dares to steal your song, the freedom you yearn for,"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"— That alone, that alone shall never do!"</color>

When Amos fired her final arrow at the tyrant, piercing the impenetrable wind barrier with her life, the King of Gales was cast from his high tower. But before the heroes who had escaped from prison could mourn their fallen comrades, a wild storm gathered, fraught with malice to engulf all who were granted a new life. Even the frailest of gods, clinging to resentment as their end nears, can topple the mightiest strongholds wrought by mortal hands, let alone the God Kings, whose might could sever frost and snow, cleave mountains asunder with winds of wrath, and fell drakes with a single arrow. Just as hope newly kindled upon the ruins seemed destined to be devoured by the wrathful storm, a moment before the annihilation was about to strike, the frail silhouette of a boy appeared at the foot of the tower. A youth, whose very body became the instrument, strummed strings that once belonged solely to the Master of Time, transforming a fleeting storm into a thousand-year-long poem. This symphony is called Mondstadt, and all who hold freedom in their hearts are its musicians. But the youth's flesh and blood could not carry the weight of a nation's song, and the bard's body fell with the collapsing tower, and his name was swept away by the winds of time. Only that tiny wind spirit, when the Mother of Time and Wind bestowed a part of her authority to it, claimed a strand of time from bygone days, along with the name that even the reversal of years could not save.

<color=#ffffffd9>"My dear friend, take now this breeze of a thousand years, and with it, a yearning for joy, and dreams of liberty."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Do not grieve for me. While the winds still blow, folk shall sing as I once did, of their hope for tomorrow."</color>

With the crumbling of an ancient seat of divinity, a new god was born — the wind spirit, Barbatos. He felt power flowing at his fingertips. His first use of this power was to reconstitute himself in the likeness of that young bard. Gunnhildr decorated the victorious Barbatos with laurels, crowning him as the Anemo Archon.
